guidance: Planning estimate—check conditions, equipment instructions, and appropriate qualified safety guidance before an activity.
method: Walking time = distance / base speed + ascent / 600 m per hour, which is Naismith's rule (1892): each 600 m of total ascent adds one hour to the flat-ground walking time. Base speed is the flat-ground pace, defaulting to 5 km/h and limited to 1-8 km/h; distance is limited to 0.1-100 km and ascent to 0-10,000 m, with metric or imperial input converted exactly. An optional 24-hour HH:MM start adds a rounded arrival that rolls past midnight. Descents, rests, rough terrain, altitude, heat and group pace are not modelled, so the result is a moving-time floor rather than a schedule; treat it as a planning estimate and add margin. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: A. A. Naismith, Cruach Ardran, Stobinian and Ben More, Scottish Mountaineering Club Journal, 1892 (Naismith's rule)
